title: Embedding endpoint: reduce p99 tail via burst smoothing and kernel fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Production embeddings endpoints show intermittent p99 spikes during short bursty traffic (small concurrent requests arriving within 50–200ms windows). Profiling on 4xA10 instances indicates these spikes correlate with: (1) uneven GPU occupancy when micro-batches materialize late, (2) occasional kernel selection that favors high-precision kernels with long launch/setup times for small micro-batches, and (3) KV cache thrash when many distinct prefixes arrive concurrently.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end p99 embedding latency on the hosted embeddings endpoint by 40–60% for common production traffic mixes (target: p99 < 220ms at steady-state tenant load used in our benchmarking harness) without increasing average token cost by more than 10%. Maintain or improve quality (embedding cosine similarity within 0.5% of baseline for representative eval set).

Scope: Engineering work on request admission/smoothing, micro-batch shaping, kernel-selection heuristics, and a controlled fallback path to lower-latency quantized kernels when calibration indicates safe quality. This ticket includes integration tests, perf dashboards, and a canary rollout plan for dedicated customers.

Out-of-scope: Major model changes or retraining, changes to client SDKs beyond optional flags, or full redesign of the runtime planner (that would be a follow-up if experiments show large gains).
acceptance_criteria: p99 on canonical synthetic workload decreases from ~420ms to <220ms under the canary config on 4xA10 (bench harness: embeddings-2026-03-canonical)
No more than 10% increase in average per-request GPU utilization and token cost across the same harness
Integration tests cover kernel-fallback path and admissions smoothing with deterministic simulation of burst arrivals
Quality regression on the evaluation suite (docs-sim-5000) is <0.5% average cosine change compared to baseline
Canary rollout plan documented and automated; rollback path validated via load-test and smoke-checks
tasks: Instrument end-to-end traces with additional tags: admission_bucket, kernel_version_hint, kv_cache_hit_ratio
Implement admission controller: burst-smoothing window (default 120ms) + priority queue for low-latency micro-batches
Add kernel fallback: detect long-launch kernels for small micro-batches and switch to quantized int8 path with per-tenant calibration cache
KV cache prefetch heuristic: detect high-cardinality prefixes and pre-warm shard-local prefix cache
Create perf job and dashboard: embeddings/p99/burst-smooth-experiments
Run canary on two dedicated tenants, capture metrics and quality evals, and iterate
